history.summary: This is a DISTINCT Tirunelveli shrine, NOT the famous Kanchipuram Divya Desam (seq 2226, id varadaraja-perumal-kancheepuram). Located at Meenakshipuram (Melaveeraragavapuram) on the banks of the Thamirabarani river, about 1 km from Tirunelveli railway station. The moolavar is Veeraraghavan and the utsavar (festival deity) is Sri Varadharaja Perumal, after whom the temple is named. Speciality: Lord Anjaneya stands in worshipping form in front of the presiding deity Veeraraghava. The corridor-prakaram holds shrines for Mahalakshmi, Sudarshanar, Bhoomadevi, Vishvaksenar, the Alwars and Lord Krishna; there are two separate shrines for Vedavalli Thayar and Perundevi Thayar. Legend: a king Krishnavarma found an idol made of blue stone while bathing in the Thamirabarani river.

name: Varadharaja Perumal Temple
town_description: Tirunelveli is a major city in southern Tamil Nadu on the banks of the Thamirabarani river, known for its twin-town character (Tirunelveli-Palayamkottai), the Nellaiappar-Kanthimathi Amman Shaivite temple, Iruttu Kadai halwa, and as a gateway to Courtallam and Kanyakumari.

travel.airport: Tuticorin (Thoothukudi) Airport, about 45 km away, is the nearest; Madurai International Airport (~150 km) is the larger alternative.
travel.railway: Tirunelveli Junction, about 1 km from the temple (Melappalayam station ~1.5 km), is the nearest major rail hub.
travel.road: 58A Sivapuram Street, Meenakshipuram, Tirunelveli 627001; on the Thamirabarani river bank, with local buses and autos from Tirunelveli town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; April-May for the 10-day Chithirai festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM-11:00 AM and 6:00 PM-8:30 PM daily (Saturday 6:00-9:00 PM) - minor differences between sources, verify locally.
